gen-fs-rx-100-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans stands tall, its lowercase sturdy and large. Over a stretch of text, the crowded tubing of RX100 would feel heavy, so brief copy is where this pairing works.
gen-fs-rx-100-fs-nunito: RX100 runs crowded and futuristic, with zero stroke contrast and a dominant x-height. Nunito follows with big round bowls and terminals that stop well clear of the stem, friendly enough for a few paragraphs.
gen-fs-rx-100-fs-quicksand: Tight and techy up top, glassy and round below: RX100 crams its letters while Quicksand lifts tall, bulb-shaped bowls. Quicksand's bars stay uniform, though long paragraphs aren't its job.
gen-fs-rx-100-fs-ranade: RX100 draws every line with zero contrast and packs them tight. Ranade loosens things with wide spacing, far-apart stroke ends and slightly shifting weight, gentle enough for a quick read.
gen-fs-rx-100-fs-supreme: Supreme sets a thick, heavy strip of crisp text. Next to RX100, whose diagonals weigh as much as its verticals, it keeps its letters open, which is why brief copy suits it.
gen-fs-rx-100-manrope: RX100 sits tight and futuristic up top, every stroke drawn without any modulation. But Manrope opens each curve wide and keeps one line width throughout, which suits brief copy.
gen-fs-rx-100-montserrat: Tight meets spacious: RX100 crowds its letters into a stocky line while Montserrat leaves generous white space before every curve. One hits hard and tight; the other glides along for a few lines.
gen-fs-rx-100-satoshi: Satoshi soars, its x-height high and its e never squeezed shut. Beneath the crowded, contrast-free RX100, those open shapes and single-width strokes are the real draw, pleasant for a paragraph or two.
gen-fs-rx-100-work-sans: Tight and futuristic: RX100 packs its letters with no stroke contrast and a dominant x-height. And Work Sans, with c tips held apart and a high mean line, is made for brief reading.
gen-fs-segment-archivo: Archivo reads editorial and friendly, its curves opening outward under a tall x-height. And Segment, stocky and widely spaced, adds the commanding presence, though modest amounts read most comfortably.
gen-fs-segment-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Wide-spaced and stocky, Segment announces itself with a tall middle band. Be Vietnam Pro follows in a plain sans with curve endings held well apart, comfortable in small doses.
gen-fs-segment-fs-familjen-grotesk: Segment spaces its letters far apart and packs them with a tall middle band, which gives lines a stocky look. Familjen Grotesk is lively sans-serif text with bowls left open on one side, though it isn't meant for long paragraphs.
gen-fs-segment-fs-supreme: Wide, stocky and commanding, Segment makes its entrance. Supreme backs it with a crisp, heavy-looking sans whose letters stay held open, which makes the pair feel made for short stretches of reading.
gen-fs-segment-satoshi: Satoshi reads tall and open, with a soaring x-height and an e that never squeezes shut. Segment is its wide, stocky counterpart, and Satoshi keeps each stroke at one width, which makes the pair made for short stretches of reading.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-plein: Plein is a reliable, clean sans that channels clearly into every round letter, made for short stretches of reading. Sharpie squeezes tight and bold, while Plein stays open.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-spline-sans: Sharpie shuts its letters almost tight, leaving only a hairline crack. Spline Sans does the opposite, its curves opening wide, so the heading grabs attention while the body simply gives you room to breathe.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-synonym: Bold and expressive, Sharpie is a display face with a narrow slot of light in every letter, while Synonym keeps one constant ink line. Sharpie makes the statement; Synonym handles the sans-level follow-through.
gen-fs-sharpie-outfit: Expressive and loud, Sharpie hardly lets any light through its letters. Outfit's curves stop short of closing and its strokes bend like cable, so a few lines of it feel open beside that tight heading.
gen-fs-sharpie-space-grotesk: Bold, expressive Sharpie squeezes its letters almost shut behind a narrow slot. Space Grotesk then opens its counters like a cut reed, a geometric ribbon of constant width that feels best in modest doses.
gen-fs-stardom-archivo: Stardom stacks outsized lowercase with thick diagonals and hairline counter-strokes. Archivo steps in with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height, so the dramatic heading gets a straightforward, editorial partner on the page.
gen-fs-stardom-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Stardom swells its round letters into fat sides under hairline tops. Be Vietnam Pro, bent-steel in stroke with curve endings far apart, offers no thick-thin pulse, so a larger heading size beside it is a reasonable suggestion.
gen-fs-stardom-fs-epilogue: Stardom goes big on lowercase, with bold downstrokes and hairline upstrokes. Epilogue's wire-like monoline skeleton and unclamped curves make the biggest difference, since nothing in it swells or thins.
gen-fs-stardom-fs-fira-sans: Fat stems like cut ribbon beside hairlines like thread give Stardom its drama. Fira Sans responds with joints that meet without thinning or bulging, so the heading performs while the body just carries the text along.
gen-fs-stardom-fs-hind: Stardom's bold stress against hairline counterstrokes is the first thing the eye catches, and its lowercase is huge. Hind stays steady, a drawn-string line with no swell at its corners.
gen-fs-stardom-fs-merriweather-sans: Big, dramatic lowercase with heavy diagonals and hairline joins, that's Stardom up top. And Merriweather Sans backs it with tall, sturdy letters whose open e keeps the whole line easy to take in.
gen-fs-stardom-fs-quicksand: Hairline joins between thick black stems give Stardom its dramatic bite, built for making an entrance. Quicksand does the opposite job, a single-weight line with bulb-shaped bowls that keeps text light and quiet.
gen-fs-stardom-general-sans: Heavy swells that taper into fine points make Stardom instantly recognizable, with outsized lowercase to match. General Sans keeps every stroke smooth and shadow-free, a tidy foil.
gen-fs-stardom-manrope: Manrope reads bright and approachable, with open curves and a single steady line. Stardom sits above it in bold black verticals joined by razor-thin strokes, so the drama stays in the heading while the text stays smooth.
gen-fs-stardom-satoshi: Bold pillars linked by faint wires make Stardom feel like stage lighting, huge lowercase and all. Satoshi's tall, stress-free letters would carry a longer read quietly.
gen-fs-stardom-work-sans: Stardom's bold stress against hairline counterstrokes is unmistakable, especially in its outsized lowercase letters. Work Sans meets it with one uniform stroke width and open tips.
gen-fs-striper-fs-amulya: Amulya reads contemporary and modern, with curves that keep their gaps generous and never crowd. And Striper hangs a graphic, playful headline above it, which makes the whole page feel comfortable in small doses.
gen-fs-striper-fs-spline-sans: Striper's graphic, playful letters have almost no calligraphic shading, so nothing in them steers the eye except shape. Spline Sans does the quieter work, its vertical and horizontal strokes of identical weight suiting a handful of lines.
gen-fs-striper-fs-synonym: Synonym is a clean, dependable sans, drawn as a plain stripe of constant ink with generous openings in every curve. But Striper, graphic and playful, is the livelier partner, so this pairing is not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-fs-tanker-fs-epilogue: Tanker is heavy and commanding, closing every curve inward with tiny gaps between letters. Epilogue answers with curvy, unclamped monoline letters and stubby ascender tips, an approachable plain sans that makes the contrast the pair's strongest quality.
gen-fs-tanker-fs-merriweather-sans: Merriweather Sans stands tall, its lowercase sturdy and its e opening plainly to the right. And Tanker's marker-like heading sits above it, so the thick line and the lighter text feel comfortable in small doses.
gen-fs-tanker-fs-supreme: Tanker is a heavy display face with pencil-like lines that never swell or thin, and its curves turn inward. Supreme, a crisp sans-serif, holds its letters open beneath it, comfortable in small doses.
gen-fs-tanker-satoshi: Dense, heavy letters from Tanker curl inward at every open curve, with lowercase that looks oversized beside its capitals. Satoshi opens right up, with a soaring x-height, and so the two sit apart.
gen-fs-tanker-switzer: Tanker comes in heavy and commanding, its inward-turning curves packed with barely a gap between them. But Switzer, a plain sans with wire-like letters and c tips held well apart, is not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-fs-trench-slab-mulish: Mulish draws its sans-serif letters like a blunt round-tip marker, with apertures open like a horseshoe magnet. And Trench Slab's outsized lowercase brings an industrial, modern weight over the top.
gen-fs-trench-slab-poppins: Trench Slab arrives industrial and modern, with a serif heading whose lowercase looks outsized. Yet Poppins, a sans-serif with rope-loose curves that keep their width through every turn, feels sturdy and relaxed beside it.
gen-fs-zina-fs-spline-sans: Zina swings between fat broad-nib downstrokes and threadlike upstrokes, with closed shapes that feel almost calligraphic. Spline Sans answers with open, friendly curves and uniform strokes, which makes a full page of it feel easy going.
gen-fs-zina-fs-synonym: Synonym lays down a plain stripe of constant ink with generous openings, so it reads dependably and cleanly. Zina's heavy verticals and hairline whispers sit above it; sizing it modestly would suit.
gen-fs-zina-plus-jakarta-sans: Fat downstrokes meeting threadlike upstrokes give Zina its refined, striking bite, and its letters stay mostly closed. Plus Jakarta Sans is monoline with curve endings kept well apart, so the page gets a precise, open counterweight.
gen-gf-abeezee-fs-karma: Trustworthy and a little old-fashioned, Karma's text serif letters sit tight between x-height and cap height with restrained modulation. ABeeZee's bent-tube sans letters, with no swelling anywhere, stand firmly above it.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-archivo: Archivo reads with a commanding x-height and curves that open outward, so lines feel confident and approachable. And Abyssinica SIL above it, with short ascenders over big bowls, carries over a refined, dignified quality into longer text.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-fs-asap: Asap reads with open arcs and a body height nearly matching its capitals, which makes text feel readable and plain. Abyssinica SIL's soft brush-like shifts sit above it nicely.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-fs-supreme: Supreme forms a thick, heavy-looking band of text, yet its letters stay held open rather than curling shut. Abyssinica SIL does dignified headings best; Supreme does crisp text.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-manrope: Abyssinica SIL leads with short ascenders over big bowls and curves a touch heavier than its joins, giving it a refined, dignified look. Manrope then keeps a single stroke width, so paragraphs should feel light and approachable.
gen-gf-abyssinica-sil-satoshi: Approachable from the first line, Satoshi stands on a soaring x-height with a wide e that never squeezes shut. And Abyssinica SIL does its best work in headings, where its joins slim noticeably while staying sturdy against rod-like sans letters.
gen-gf-aclonica-fs-erode: Aclonica takes the heading with a large x-height, short ascenders, and wide open space between letters, giving it a modern, professional look. Erode follows below, and a slightly larger size would suit its tall middle band.
gen-gf-aclonica-fs-karma: Karma reads as a classic serif with terminals that finish well clear of the stem and a gentle modulation that never snags the eye. Beside Aclonica, its trustworthy tone is the best part.
gen-gf-aldrich-fs-karma: Karma is a serif with terminals that finish well clear of the stem. And Aldrich, with horizontals and verticals of identical thickness like rod stock, gives that softness a firm, modern frame to lean on.
gen-gf-alexandria-fs-erode: A tall x-height you notice at a glance defines Alexandria. Erode's serif joins slim noticeably yet stay sturdy, giving the low-contrast heading a worthy, more traditional partner on the page.
gen-gf-alexandria-fs-karma: Bright and upright, Alexandria stands tall with its g open at the bottom. Karma, the classic serif, handles the quiet work, its modulation never snagging the eye, while the heading grabs attention.
gen-gf-allerta-fs-erode: Every word in Allerta stretches out wide, with a sizable x-height built for screens. Erode brings classic serif warmth, its tall middle band and gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight softening the heading's wide stance.
gen-gf-allerta-fs-karma: Allerta stretches every word wide, with a sizable x-height. Karma, a serif whose bowls swell only slightly, has little gap between x-height and cap height, so give Karma a modest size bump.
gen-gf-allerta-stencil-fs-erode: Allerta Stencil towers in a stubby x-height with spaced-out words. Let Erode, a serif of moderate contrast, run a touch larger than usual so it holds against the heading's heavy stems and thread-thin arms.
gen-gf-almendra-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Curves that never crowd their endings make the body read crisp and clean, like bent steel rod. Be Vietnam Pro handles the steady text, while Almendra brings small letters nearly matching capitals, like cut sheet-metal stencils.
gen-gf-almendra-fs-merriweather-sans: Almendra, a serif whose small letters nearly match capitals, looks like cut sheet-metal stencils. Merriweather Sans makes words look sturdy and large, its e opening clearly to the right, which keeps a full page going smoothly.
gen-gf-alumni-sans-fs-erode: Erode reads dignified and editorial, its middle band tall. Beside Alumni Sans and its tightly pressed characters, Erode's broad-mouthed g and a and gentle stroke weight carry paragraphs along without effort.
gen-gf-alumni-sans-fs-karma: Alumni Sans presses its characters close, yet opens the c wide and gives every e a large, clear eye. What lingers is Karma's classic serif modulation, never snagging the eye.
gen-gf-alumni-sans-collegiate-one-fs-kar: Alumni Sans Collegiate One stacks its glyphs tightly, with small letters nearly as tall as capitals. And Karma, a classic serif, keeps that tall-lowercase look but softens it with gentle, trustworthy strokes.
gen-gf-alumni-sans-pinstripe-fs-karma: Karma moves smoothly, its swing from thick to thin never snagging. Beside it, Alumni Sans Pinstripe feels like following one hollow thread, so the whole pairing reads in a mellow, unhurried way.
gen-gf-alumni-sans-sc-fs-erode: Capitals that stand barely taller than the lowercase give Alumni Sans SC a distinctive, compact look up top. Erode, a serif, picks up that tall middle band and adds dignity.
gen-gf-alumni-sans-sc-fs-karma: Alumni Sans SC keeps its capitals close to lowercase height. Karma, a classic serif, shares that tight height range, so the two feel like relatives with different manners.
gen-gf-amiko-fs-karma: Karma is a serif with terminals that finish well clear of the stem and a calm, moderate modulation. Under Amiko's chunky, tall midzone, it reads smoothly and without a single snag.
gen-gf-anaheim-fs-erode: Clean, tight-set letters give Anaheim a clamped, vise-grip look with rounds left unsealed. Erode, a serif with gentle stroke variation, loosens the mood, and it holds up nicely if the body text goes a bit larger.
gen-gf-anek-bangla-fs-karma: Karma reads smooth and settled, its terminals stopping well short of the stem. Anek Bangla leads with ajar-mouthed a shapes and low contrast, and page after page of this text serif would glide by without a snag.
gen-gf-anek-devanagari-fs-erode: Approachable and modern, Anek Devanagari stands up tall, its broad counters and very tall x-height making every line feel generous. Erode, a text serif, does its best work in dignified editorial flow.
gen-gf-anek-devanagari-fs-karma: A very tall x-height gives Anek Devanagari its stature, with broad open counters on c and s keeping the letters friendly. Karma, the serif, brings a soft, tilted-nib steadiness that ties it together.
gen-gf-anek-gujarati-fs-erode: Neutral and approachable, Anek Gujarati sets its midline high and cuts generous openings, like a chisel notch in wood. Erode adds dignified editorial weight with its gentle ebb and flow of stroke.
gen-gf-anek-gujarati-fs-karma: High midline, notched openings: Anek Gujarati looks cut from wood, and its mellow stroke range stays friendly. Karma, the serif, would carry pages smoothly, its terminals clear of the stems.
gen-gf-anek-gurmukhi-fs-erode: Erode reads tall and dignified, its middle band generous and its stroke weight gently ebbing and flowing. And Anek Gurmukhi matches that tall band, leaving its round letters generously unclosed while light strokes barely recede.
gen-gf-anek-gurmukhi-fs-karma: Karma sets a serif voice with terminals held clear of the stem. Anek Gurmukhi brings generously unclosed curves and a modest stroke contrast, so headings and text feel cut from related cloth.
gen-gf-anek-kannada-fs-erode: Oversized-looking small letters define Anek Kannada, whose open apertures keep every shape plainly legible. And Erode, the serif, meets it with a tall middle band and softly modulated strokes without sharp hairlines.
gen-gf-anek-kannada-fs-karma: Karma reads settled and classic, its modulation so soft that nothing snags the eye. And Anek Kannada, with oversized small letters and a middle-ground stroke contrast, keeps the serif company without competing.
gen-gf-anek-latin-fs-erode: A generously wide letter c marks Anek Latin, whose capitals and lowercase sit close in height. Erode, the serif, would read with a gentle ebb and flow, yarn to the heading's thread.
gen-gf-anek-telugu-fs-erode: Erode reads with a tall middle band and a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight, which smooths the pace. Anek Telugu does best at crisp, clog-free shapes, while Erode handles sustained reading.
gen-gf-arbutus-archivo: Dignified and a little old-fashioned, Arbutus spreads its tall lowercase wide with a mild, friendly stroke contrast. And Archivo, a plain sans with a commanding x-height, curves outward and brings an editorial directness underneath.
gen-gf-arbutus-fs-asap: Arbutus spaces its big-countered, tall lowercase far apart, with sturdy thin lines beside slightly heavier thick ones. Asap, in a plain sans, feels open and businesslike beside it.
gen-gf-arbutus-fs-epilogue: Arbutus brings thin strokes without hairlines beside moderately weighty stems, giving a dignified, classic look up top. Epilogue's wire-like sans letters run curvy and loose below.
gen-gf-arbutus-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans opens its s curves wide at both ends and draws every stroke with no thick-thin variation, with a generous x-height. But Arbutus, with its closed, spread-out letters, earns its place when the text is big and brief.
gen-gf-arbutus-fs-public-sans: Trustworthy and hefty, Public Sans sets a broad lowercase with open counters on c and s. Arbutus does its best work with slight, visible thick-thin variation and a dignified spread, while that sans plainly carries the text.
gen-gf-arbutus-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp, a thick, heavy-looking strip of sans text with letters held open. Arbutus is the one for dignified, closed shapes and mild stroke contrast, while Supreme simply keeps the lines moving.
gen-gf-arbutus-satoshi: Arbutus runs a lightly shaded texture through each word, with big counters and a tall, spread-out lowercase. Satoshi's sans-serif strokes never swell or thin, so a long read stays smooth.
gen-gf-arbutus-switzer: Arbutus has a stroke weight that shifts noticeably but never dramatically, with big counters and widely spaced letters. And Switzer, a sans-serif of rod-like, wire-thin forms, probably looks tidiest when its size stays modest.
gen-gf-archivo-narrow-fs-karma: Archivo Narrow stands deep and tall through the middle, packed tight. Karma, a classic serif, brings soft stroke shifts and terminals that stop clear of the stem, so paragraphs flow without snagging.
gen-gf-arimo-fs-erode: Erode reads dignified and editorial, its tall middle band keeping ascenders shallow. Arimo, by contrast, is stubby at the top and bottom of its letters, with wide mouths that stay open.
gen-gf-armata-fs-karma: Karma reads trustworthy and classic, with soft thickness shifts that never turn stark across a page. And Armata's generous letterspacing and open curves up top give that quiet serif a lively, modern frame.
gen-gf-arsenal-fs-karma: Trustworthy Karma, a text serif, sits low and compact in its letterforms. But Arsenal's high midline and pried-open e give the headings a crisper, cleaner edge that makes the soft body feel even calmer.
gen-gf-arsenal-sc-fs-karma: Arsenal SC packs its letters tightly, with curves that gape wide like a jar lid. And Karma, a classic serif, answers that compactness with terminals clear of the stem and a calm, steady modulation.
gen-gf-asap-condensed-fs-erode: Tightly twisted and tall in the middle, like cord fibers pulled snug. Asap Condensed grabs attention fast, while Erode, the text serif, handles the slow reading.
gen-gf-athiti-fs-erode: Wire-fine and wide open, Athiti leads with curves that end in plain daylight. Erode follows in its classic serif dress, its sturdy bowls and lightly thinned links giving the thin, even headings a grounded, editorial partner underneath.
gen-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible-fs-erode: Modern in a no-fuss way, Atkinson Hyperlegible keeps its curves smooth and its hairline thinning low. Erode, a serif with a tall middle band and modest thinning, adds a dignified, editorial voice below.
gen-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible-fs-karma: Atkinson Hyperlegible keeps a short stretch from midline to ascender, so its bends run smooth and unobstructed. And Karma, a text serif, does the opposite job, its soft accents of heavier strokes giving a long read a steady, classic rhythm.
gen-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible-next-fs-ero: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next spreads its curve ends wide and lifts its x-height close to the cap height, which feels modern and businesslike. Erode's classic serif strokes then keep a long page moving gently.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-bitter: Bitter has a very large lowercase and an s you can see right through, which makes paragraphs feel sturdy and unhurried. Bitter also lets the stencil-cut weight of Balsamiq Sans stand out as the loud one.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-inter: Chunky and cheerful, then smooth as a tube. Balsamiq Sans is the one to make noise with, and Inter is the one that stays readable with its big counters and tall lowercase.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-mulish: Approachable from the first line, since Balsamiq Sans carries a stencil-cut weight with no tight, pinched curves. Mulish then keeps a long page easy on the eye, with open horseshoe apertures and no thick-and-thin modulation.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-poppins: Poppins reads with rope-loose curves and a tall, sturdy lowercase, never flickering between thick and thin strokes. And Balsamiq Sans, with its stencil-cut weight, gives the pair a bold, expressive streak.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-roboto-slab: Precise and structured, Roboto Slab fills the middle of each line, while Balsamiq Sans has horizontals and verticals as uniform as rod stock. That difference in lowercase height is the pair's hook.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-rubik: Soft and friendly, Rubik sets lowercase that looks big beside its capitals, with round shapes that stay clear. Balsamiq Sans adds lines that hold their thickness, so the heading looks bolder and more playful than the quieter body beneath it.
gen-gf-basic-fs-erode: Erode reads with a tall middle band, shallow ascenders and a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight. Yet Basic, with its high squared-off x-height, supplies the crisp sans-serif front, and the mix of styles is the real draw.
gen-gf-basic-fs-karma: Karma finishes its terminals well clear of the stem and keeps its modulation gentle enough never to snag the eye. And Basic, with its high squared-off x-height, gives that trustworthy serif body a crisp, modern sans-serif lead-in.
gen-gf-baumans-bitter: Baumans draws every stroke at one thickness, with a c like a wrench opened wide, and that is where it does its best work. Bitter handles the other job, with its big lowercase and open s keeping text dependable.
gen-gf-baumans-instrument-sans: Crescent-wrench curves in a single line weight: that is Baumans, striking and unmistakable up top. And Instrument Sans, a plain sans, carries page after page smoothly, its stroke weight never wavering.
gen-gf-baumans-inter: Wide-open crescent curves, one line weight throughout: that is Baumans. But the real hook is height, with Baumans staying moderate while Inter, a sans, stands tall in the lowercase.
gen-gf-baumans-mulish: Blunt, wrench-wide curves: Baumans draws every stroke in a single line width, while Mulish, a sans, has a large x-height. Size Mulish down a notch, since its lowercase already runs tall.
gen-gf-baumans-poppins: Poppins, a plain sans, reads with loose, rope-like curves that never snag the eye, its tall lowercase carrying the text beneath Baumans. Page after page it should glide without snagging.
gen-gf-baumans-roboto-slab: Commanding from the first letter, Baumans draws a wrench-wide c in one line width. Roboto Slab, a slab-serif, stays precise across a full page, its open throats keeping the middle of each line crisp.
gen-gf-baumans-rubik: Baumans draws uniform lines with no heavier downstrokes, a wrench-open c leading the way with real presence. But Rubik, a sans-serif with soft, round letters, does its best work at small sizes.
gen-gf-bayon-fs-karma: Glyphs fused almost like a stencil make Bayon unmistakable, uniform strokes up top, while Karma, a serif, brings gentle weight shifts below. Paragraphs in it read trustworthy and settled, with nothing snagging the eye.
gen-gf-bellota-bitter: Bellota's s throws its ends far from the spine, which gives the heading its commanding swagger. But Bitter, a slab-serif with a very large lowercase eye, is the one built to carry the text.
gen-gf-bellota-inter: Far-flung s-ends, stylus-width lines: Bellota is hard to mistake for anything else. Inter, a sans with generous counters and a high lowercase, reads smoothly through pages of text, each line tube-smooth.
gen-gf-bellota-mulish: Distinctive from the first letter, Bellota hangs the ends of its s far from the spine and draws every stroke like a stylus. Mulish takes over with horseshoe-open shapes and no thick-thin shading, which keeps the page friendly.
gen-gf-bellota-poppins: Poppins reads smooth and sturdy, with loose curves and no flicker of thick and thin. Bellota above it is the surprise, its stylus-traced strokes and far-hanging s giving the pair a commanding, slightly odd edge.
gen-gf-bellota-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab reads precise and structured, its middle zone dominating each line with open throats on a, c, e and s. Bellota adds a distinctive, stylus-drawn voice on top, and its lowercase sits lower than the slab-serif beneath.
gen-gf-bellota-text-bitter: Bitter reads grounded and dependable, its huge lowercase eye and see-through s making each line easy to follow. Bellota Text is the blunt, marker-tipped voice above it, so a slightly larger heading gives that round-tipped feel room to carry.
gen-gf-bellota-text-instrument-sans: Instrument Sans brings pincer-open c shapes, a minimal step down from capitals and strokes that never vary in weight. Bellota Text, commanding and shading-free, sits above it with a lower lowercase.
gen-gf-bellota-text-inter: Round, open and quietly commanding, Bellota Text leads with no calligraphic shading at all. And Inter, a plain sans with hollow-reed counters and a tall lowercase, lets that heading earn its keep when it runs big and short.
gen-gf-bellota-text-poppins: Bellota Text looks open and commanding, with no calligraphic shading, and sits low in its lowercase above a tall, sturdy body. Poppins lets long reading run smoothly, its curves loose and unknotted.
gen-gf-bellota-text-roboto-slab: Commanding at the top, Bellota Text uses open shapes with no calligraphic shading to guide the eye. Roboto Slab, a slab-serif with open throats and a dominant middle zone, makes a long stretch feel structured and precise.
gen-gf-bellota-text-rubik: Bellota Text has no calligraphic shading, just one fixed nib width and open, friendly curves. Rubik follows with soft, large-looking lowercase, so paragraphs feel rounded and easy going.
gen-gf-biryani-fs-erode: Contemporary and wiry, Biryani draws tubular letters whose tiny counters never clog up. Erode takes over with a tall middle band and a gentle swell of stroke weight, so longer paragraphs read dignified and unhurried.
gen-gf-black-han-sans-fs-karma: Dense, sprawling and nearly closed, Black Han Sans hits hard with low stress, while Karma uses mild stress and calm modulation. Paragraphs in the classic serif stay smooth and trustworthy.
gen-gf-braah-one-fs-erode: Modern and clean, Braah One squeezes its s nearly shut and looks magnified even at modest sizes. And Erode, a dignified serif, opens its g and a broadly, doing the quieter work of carrying the text.
gen-gf-braah-one-fs-karma: Karma reads as a trustworthy serif, with terminals that finish clear of the stem and very little gap between x-height and cap height. And Braah One, with its magnified look, deserves a bit more room than the body.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-instrument-sans: Ruler-straight and unhurried, Bruno Ace lets every character take its own beat. Instrument Sans, a plain sans with a lower, modest lowercase, follows without competing, keeping its strokes uniform beneath the heading.
